_meta.simulation_note: Simulated state as of 2026-08-10 (Sprint 20 Day 1). Milestones closed since Jun 28: ATLAS M8 GA soft launch (Jun 30), NEXUS M6 IAM (Jul 1, 1 day late), NEXUS M5 CI/CD (Jul 3, 3 days late), SHIELD M4 100 controls (Jul 15, on time), SHIELD M5 the auditor evidence (Jul 15 → reopened Jul 16 on evidence-sufficiency findings → re-closed Aug 7), HORIZON M6 beta 10 customers (Jul 22, 7 days late), HORIZON M7 App Store submission (Aug 1, on time), PULSE M4 FlowEngine (Aug 7, 13 days late). Missed: MERIDIAN M6 mid-market (Aug 1 → revised Aug 21). Decisions DR-011 through DR-015 applied. SHIELD M6 restated per DR-014: Aug 31 is audit-readiness, Type II report Dec 15. SPARK M2 due Aug 11 at 88% — the open item at the export boundary. Full event ledger: 1-inputs-triggers/simulation-log.json.

programs.name: NEXUS — Platform Re-architecture & Service Consolidation
programs.ragRationale: M5 ✅ Jul 3 and M6 ✅ Jul 1 both closed. IAM deployed Jun 30 22:05; token-refresh latency spike Jul 2 patched same day; hypercare exited clean Jul 10 with no further incidents. Everything that was gated on NEXUS — HORIZON beta, 14 SHIELD controls, ATLAS full-IAM planning (DEP-002, started Jul 13) — is now unblocked. First solid green since Q1. Remaining scope is M7 (service count <200) against a Dec 31 target, currently tracking.

programs.name: ATLAS — Enterprise NovaAI Launch
programs.ragRationale: M8 GA soft launch ✅ Jun 30. The July story is uptime: GA load pushed rolling uptime to 96.8% on Jul 6, below the 97% internal floor. Leo Nakamura chose to protect the SLA over the milestone (DR-011) — emergency capacity plus a rate limit on new tenant onboarding. Circuit breaker (F6) shipped Jul 31 and uptime recovered to 98.9%. July month average 97.1% against a 99.0% commitment — missed, and communicated honestly. Rate limit lifted Aug 3. Cost of the decision: M7 frozen at 3/5 enterprise customers for four weeks, target moved to Sep 15. Green because the platform is sound and the tradeoff was deliberate.

programs.name: SHIELD — SOC 2 Type II Certification
programs.ragRationale: M4 CLOSED Jul 15 ✅ — all 100 controls complete, on time. The 14 IAM-blocked controls closed Jul 11–14 once NEXUS IAM went live. M5 evidence package delivered Jul 15, then REOPENED Jul 16: The auditor failed 3 controls on operating-effectiveness grounds — log retention (closed Jun 30) and 2 IAM controls live only since Jul 1 carry days of operating history, not months. Remediated and re-closed Aug 7. That finding forced the certification-date question into the open (DR-014): the Aug 31 board mandate is AUDIT-READINESS, not certification. Observation period Sep 1 – Nov 30, Type II report Dec 15. Amber because readiness is confirmed but the three-month observation window is a different discipline from building controls — any drift restarts the clock.

milestones.name: Audit evidence package to the auditor
milestones.ragNote: Delivered on time Jul 15, REOPENED Jul 16, re-closed Aug 7. The auditor's review failed 3 of 100 controls on evidence sufficiency: A1.7 (log retention policy) and CC6.4/CC6.6 (IAM access review, IAM privileged access) had insufficient operating history for Type II. Remediation Jul 20 – Aug 5: re-collected evidence with 30+ days of operating history where available, compensating documentation for the IAM pair. The auditor confirmed sufficiency Aug 7.

milestones.name: SOC 2 Type II audit readiness (board mandate)

The board accepted the restatement: Aug 31 is readiness. Path: M4 ✅ → M5 ✅ Aug 7 → readiness sign-off Aug 31 → observation Sep 1 – Nov 30 → report Dec 15.

programs.name: MERIDIAN — API Consolidation & v1 Deprecation
programs.ragRationale: M6 MISSED Aug 1 at 202/210 (96%). Compass Migration Partners flexed onto mid-market Jul 17 once SMB passed 90%, which moved 30 customers in three weeks — the plan worked, it just started too late to close the gap. The remaining 8 are the long tail: complex bespoke integrations that self-service tooling cannot reach. DR-015 assigned dedicated engineering support and a revised Aug 21 target. M7 (v1 EoL Sep 30) sits directly behind M6 with five weeks of margin — tight but intact.

programs.name: PULSE — Data Pipeline Overhaul (Airflow → Temporal)
programs.ragRationale: M4 FlowEngine CLOSED Aug 7 ✅ — 340/340 pipelines migrated, 13 days late against the revised Jul 25 target. PULSE is off red for the first time since Q1. The DR-009 reallocation worked: Sprint 17 closed at 22 items against the ~20 needed, and the Jul 10 checkpoint chose to continue without descoping (DR-013). The 13-day slip came from the last 27 pipelines, which were the most entangled in the estate. Total dual-run cost $1.38M against the $1.2M projection — $180K over, and now stopped. Amber not green: M6 Airflow decommission (Sep 30) is now the critical path and has never been started.

programs.ragRationale: M6 CLOSED Jul 22 ✅ — 10 enterprise beta customers, 7 days late. The dedicated onboarding engineer (DR-012, approved Jul 8) took 4/10 to 10/10 in two weeks; the decision was correct but came two weeks too late to hold Jul 15. Soft GA delivered on time Jul 31 per DR-008. M7 submission made Aug 1 on time — Android approved Aug 6, iOS still in review with a decision expected Aug 15–22. Amber for one reason: the Aug 31 public GA now depends on Apple, which is outside the program's control.

programs.name: SPARK — NovaAI v2 Core Platform
